newsitem.title: LATVIA: AGENCY SAYS UNIBANKA, ZEMES SHOULD STILL MERGE.
newsitem.headline: AGENCY SAYS UNIBANKA, ZEMES SHOULD STILL MERGE.

text.p: The Latvian Privatisation Agency (LPA) maintains its view that Unibanka and Zemes Bank would be more able to beat the competition by merging, an LPA official was quoted as saying on Thursday by daily newspaper Diena.

LPA, the largest Unibanka shareholder as it controls the state's 33.33 percent, has not changed its position in the merger issue, LPA legal manager Viktor Shadinov was quoted in the newspaper as saying.
The newspaper pointed out that The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD), who owns a stake in both banks, has expressed a conflicting opinion.
Both the LPA and the EBRD have an agreement to have an identical vote on all substantial issues in general meetings, Shadinov was quoted as saying.
Leading Latvian Bank Unibanka and Zemes Bank announced on Tuesday about the cancellation of their merger plan and that they will continue to work as separate finacial institutions.
The LPA was not invited to the March 25 meeting, which decided on the cancellation of the merger although the EBRD representative was present.
Shadinov was quoted as saying that the agreement between the LPA and the EBRD has to be changed as one of the parties had violated it.
An Unibanka general meeting on April 21 is scheduled to discuss the merger and the LPA can influence its decision due to its 33 percent stake.
LPA has not yet been acquainted with the reasons behind the cancellation decision, Shadinov was quoted as saying.
